Models use both classes, but the study compares architectures/representations and extrapolation tasks, not a matched ablation isolating negative-label contribution. CPI models often fail to beat single-task baselines; AUPRC is used because AUROC can overvalue true negatives. Direct relevance 3/3 to assay-grounded negative use and evaluation design; does not establish standalone value or literature-wide recovery.

query_text: Audit how ESP validates its generated enzyme-substrate negatives and whether its reported test performance proves those negative labels are biologically correct
source: Inspect Kroll et al. 2023 primary article for negative generation rules, splitting, independent test composition, acknowledged label noise, and any experimentally measured negative holdout
notes: ESP samples three structurally similar putative negatives per experimentally confirmed positive from a restricted metabolite set, then splits the constructed data with enzyme sequence identity capped at 80%. The independent test therefore evaluates labels generated using the same sampling procedure; the article acknowledges potential false negatives but no experimentally adjudicated negative holdout or measured-vs-generated negative ablation was identified. Strong evidence for large-scale model feasibility under proxy-negative assumptions, not validation of those assumptions. Relevance 3/3 to negative construction/evaluation design, 0/3 direct evidence for the value of literature-recovered measured negatives.

query_text: Determine whether prior negative-example-quality studies show downstream model value and whether their labels are assay-grounded molecular negatives
source: Read Youngs et al. 2014 NoGO primary article; distinguish predicted GO negatives from measured assay outcomes, inspect temporal validation and downstream function-prediction comparison
notes: NoGO predicts negatives from GO positive-annotation structure under an open-world/PU assumption. It evaluates false negatives using temporal future GO annotations (2010 training, 2012 validation) and reports fewer errors for SNOB/NETL/Rocchio than random/heuristic selection; downstream GO prediction with selected negatives outperforms random-negative selection across human/mouse/yeast, with an Arabidopsis case using 313,592 predicted negatives. This directly supports quality-dependent utility of inferred negatives in protein-function ML, but is not evidence about experimentally measured molecular activity negatives or literature recovery. Relevance 2/3 to utility theory, 0/3 direct assay-recovery evidence.

query_text: Audit whether Goldman et al. glycosyltransferase benchmark converts untested source cells into negative labels
source: Clone the official enzyme-datasets repository; inspect README semantics, pinned reformat_gts.py logic, and released categorical/binary donor and acceptor files
notes: At commit 627556e265e2a52d39753e684c05b550d53a9be4 the parser exports only spreadsheet values != 0; source class 1 maps to binary inactive 0, while 2/3 map active. Audited achiral donor counts: source categories 361/12/141, binary 361/153; acceptor 3460/266/572, binary 3460/838. Thus README-described untested 0 cells are omitted rather than misclassified as inactive; released CSV lacks an explicit missingness mask, and raw workbooks were unavailable in repository. Relevance 3/3 to label semantics, 2/3 to literature-recovery scope; no negative-specific ML ablation.

query_text: Determine whether a public plant UGT donor-specificity compilation already preserves literature-derived inactive reaction labels and how those labels are defined
source: Download Zenodo record 16761161 CSV; count outcomes, source DOI coverage and duplicate reaction keys; inspect the linked 2024 review and repository-level curation/conflict rules
notes: CSV contains 1,189 rows (590 activity=0, 599 activity=1), 218 enzymes, 10 donors and 110 acceptor strings; every row carries one DOI, though 7 reaction keys repeat and none conflict in outcome. Zenodo describes 108 acceptors, resolves any source conflict toward active, and defines <5% of each enzyme's strongest reaction as inactive. Thus this is direct narrow-domain prior art for literature-compiled UGT binary activity labels, but not a context-complete or raw-measurement archive; individual zero labels need DOI-level audit. DOI 10.3389/fbioe.2024.1396268 is a review and this is its supplementary compilation, not an extraction benchmark. Relevance 3/3 to novelty/provenance; 0/3 direct independent ML utility evidence.

query_text: Trace the largest source represented in the curated UGT literature dataset back to its primary assay matrix and test what the aggregate inactive label can substantiate
source: Group Zenodo rows by DOI 10.1038/s41589-018-0154-9; inspect Yang et al. 2018 Supplementary Figure 3 legend/caption and compare source panel dimensions, outcomes, and repeat design
notes: This source contributes 278 aggregate rows: 168 activity=0 and 110 activity=1 for 49 GT1s × six donors × Kaempferol. Supplementary Figure 3 defines red S/N<1, amber S/N 1-10 and green S/N>10; caption says high-throughput GAR experiments were single measurements. The processed repository skips source class 0 (untested per README) and encodes source class 1 as binary inactive, but no complete pixel-to-row crosswalk was done. Supports assay-grounded provenance for a major source while exposing absent replication and retained raw-value/context limitations; do not generalize beyond this DOI. Relevance 3/3 to source-linkage, 0/3 direct model utility.

query_text: Audit a second UGT compilation source at one exact inactive reaction row, including donor context and any internal source-paper label conflict
source: For DOI 10.1093/pcp/pcx081, join the Zenodo UGT88A13/Gal/Quercetin zero record to primary Table 1, its footnote, Results and enzymatic assay methods
notes: The matching row is activity=0; primary Table 1 gives UGT88A13/quercetin as UDP-Glc 3′-O product and UDP-Gal not detectable (3′ (–)); footnote defines dash as no detectable product. Methods specify 10 µg protein, 30°C, pH 7.5, 0.5mM acceptor, 4mM donor and 30min HPLC, but do not state enzyme-screen replicate count. Abstract/discussion contradict Results/Table 1 on UGT88A13 activity toward kaempferol/quercetin. This validates one condition-bound negative and exposes intra-paper conflict; remaining 30 source DOI zeros not audited. Relevance 3/3 to provenance/context, 0/3 independent model utility.

query_text: Audit a third UGT compilation source by matching exact inactive donor/acceptor rows to source text and checking whether assay replication/context survive
source: For DOI 10.1105/tpc.18.00641, group Zenodo rows; match AsAAT1/TCP/UDP-Glc and UDP-Gal zeros to Louveau et al. Results and Figure 3A caption; record signal readout and replicates
notes: The source contributes 32 Zenodo rows (20 binary zeros, 12 ones; 10 enzyme labels, four donors, three acceptor names). Two exact rows, AsAAT1/TCP/Glc=0 and Gal=0, match source text saying no detectable product with those donors while UDP-Ara is preferred/active. Figure 3A monitors TCP glycoside at 405 nm and reports three biological replicates with SD. No LOD/threshold found in checked passage; remaining 18 source DOI zeros not individually mapped; aggregate CSV loses raw activity and replicate values. Relevance 3/3 to provenance/context and 2/3 to recovery feasibility; 0/3 direct ML utility.

query_text: Audit a fourth UGT compilation source for DOI-level matrix coverage and match every compiled inactive row to the source supplement
source: For DOI 10.3389/fpls.2022.863482, count compiled reaction cells; compare all 20 zeros to official Supplementary Tables S5/S6 and record ND definition, replicate count, and cells absent from the source grid
notes: Zenodo group has 33 rows (20 zero, 13 one), 2 enzymes × 4 donors × 5 represented acceptors; seven of those 40 cells are absent, and the source supplement also tested a sixth acceptor (malvidin), leaving 15/48 full-grid cells absent from the compilation. All 20 binary zeros match S5/S6 entries marked ND (not detected due to low activity); activity values are means of three independent determinations. S6 reports Rd3GT6/delphinidin UDP-Rha 8.49±0.42% and UDP-Ara ND, matching its compiled UDP-Ara zero; Results' 5.96% cyanidin UDP-Ara statement aligns, while Discussion wording is ambiguous when read as a full cross-product. Absent cells remain unknown, not inactive; CSV loses numeric activities and replicates. Relevance 3/3 to provenance/context/missingness and 2/3 recovery feasibility; 0/3 direct ML utility.

query_text: Trace the CsUGT76F1 negative donor/acceptor records in a fifth cited UGT source back to explicit substrate-specificity statements and recover protocol context
source: For DOI 10.3389/fpls.2018.00166, group the 20 Zenodo rows; compare all 13 zeros with Results on UDP-Rha acceptor scope and alternative UDP donors; capture assay conditions without conflating specificity-screen replicates with kinetic replicates
notes: The group has 20 rows (13 zero, 7 one) over five acceptors/four donors. Results state that CsUGT76F1 uses UDP-Rha to rhamnosylate quercetin/kaempferol, not hesperetin/naringenin/diosmetin, and only accepts UDP-Rha among alternative donors tested; this matches the three Rha zeros plus ten Gal/Xyl zeros. Standard enzyme assay: 50 μL, 100 mM Tris-HCl pH7.5, 2.5 mM donor, 0.2 mM acceptor, 20 μg protein, 30°C, 1h, UPLC-Q-TOF-MS. Kinetic parameters are based on three independent experiments, but the specificity-matrix replicate count and detection limit were not found. Do not transfer kinetic n=3 to specificity rows. Relevance 3/3 to provenance/context, 2/3 to recovery feasibility, 0/3 direct ML utility.

query_text: Correct convenience sampling in the UGT source audit by defining a fixed-seed stratified sample
source: Group the 103 remaining source DOIs by compilation record count (1–4, 5–9, 10–19, 20+); use seed 20260930 to draw two source DOIs from each stratum and retain the complete frame and selected list
notes: The frame contains 48, 35, 15 and 5 sources in the four respective strata. Selected: 10.1042/BCJ20200477; 10.1371/journal.pone.0075268; 10.1039/D0QO00579G; 10.1111/nph.14039; 10.1007/s12374-018-0103-x; 10.1039/C8CC04215B; 10.1021/acs.orglett.9b00524; 10.1016/j.fitote.2021.104995. This corrects selection among easy/high-volume sources but 8/103 is not a population estimate and inherits compilation scope bias.

query_text: Audit the first fixed-sample PLOS UGT73C14 source for row-level negative evidence versus panel-level conclusion
source: For DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0075268, compare the three DOI-group records against Results, Enzyme Assays and Figure S5 caption; record exact donor/acceptor row, tested panel, method, controls, and limits on mapping
notes: Three compilation rows (2 active, 1 inactive); zero is UGT73C14/UDP-glucuronic acid/ABA. Source reports ABA glycosylation with UDP-glucose/UDP-galactose and tests three donors including UDP-glucuronic acid across acceptors; conditions 5 μg enzyme, 100 μL, 50mM Tris pH8, 50mM MgCl2, 500μM ATP, 2.5mM UDP-sugar, 250μM acceptor, 30°C, 2.5h, HPLC-MS, no-enzyme controls. No per-cell value, LOD, or explicit exact-cell statement found; separate kinetic technical replicates do not establish screen n. Classify exact zero as aggregate label compatible with broader source conclusion, not fully row-verified. Relevance 3/3 provenance/context, 2/3 feasibility, 0/3 independent ML utility.

query_text: Audit the second fixed-sample source for exact donor-specific negative pairs in a plant UGT screen
source: Normalize and exactly match DOI 10.1042/BCJ20200477 in the Zenodo CSV; inspect the three AtUGT76D1/quercetin donor rows against the primary paper Results, Figure 1B legend and assay Methods
notes: Exact DOI-field match returns UDP-Glc=1, UDP-Gal=0 and UDP-GlcNAc=0 for AtUGT76D1/quercetin. Source explicitly reports no 76D1 activity with UDP-Gal and donor specificity text/Figure 1B supports no UDP-GlcNAc activity (red=no activity); method is 1mM Tris/1mM MgCl2 pH8, 10mM donor and acceptor, purified enzyme, 37°C 15h, LC-MS. Analyses were done in duplicates; independence unclear. A substring query falsely returned 11 rows by including eight co-cited DOI-field entries; these were excluded by exact match. Relevance 3/3 provenance/context, 2/3 recovery feasibility, 0/3 independent ML benefit.

query_text: Attempt primary-source retrieval for the next two DOI groups selected by the fixed stratified sample
source: Check official RSC full-text/SI for DOI 10.1039/D0QO00579G and Wiley full-text/SI for DOI 10.1111/nph.14039; try public PMC/Europe PMC routes; record access failures without inferring source outcomes
notes: RSC publisher page confirms the source and official 4.7MB SI link, but browser retrieval of the PDF was blocked as restricted and guessed direct paths returned 404. Wiley page confirms article and SI including Figure S14 on GuUGAT donor specificity, but full-text/SI links were restricted; PMC returned a CAPTCHA and Europe PMC XML returned HTTP 500. Exact Zenodo field groups have 7 rows/3 zeros for RSC and 6 rows/4 zeros for Wiley; these remain compilation-only labels until source review. Continue with other sampled sources; revisit these if publisher/repository access changes.

query_text: Trace six compiled Sb3GT1 donor-specific zeros to the source paper's supporting chromatograms
source: Download the free ACS Figshare SI for DOI 10.1021/acs.orglett.9b00524; exact-match the Zenodo DOI rows; map each UDP-Gal zero to its compound number and inspect the corresponding HPLC trace in Figures S10/S11/S14/S15/S16/S19; recover assay conditions and limitations
notes: The exact DOI group has 66 rows and six zeros, all UDP-Gal paired with Fisetin, Icaritin, Morin, Kaempferide, 3-Hydroxyflavone, or Kaempferol 4'-glucoside (compounds 7,8,11,12,13,16). Each corresponding HPLC trace shows substrate without the matching glycosylated-product peak; other donor traces support conditional specificity. Assay: 50mM Tris-HCl pH9, 4μg enzyme, 0.1mM acceptor, 0.5mM donor, 45°C, 1h, HPLC/MS. No screen-specific LOD or replicate count found. SI retained locally; source supports feasibility, not prevalence or ML gain.

query_text: Audit whether CtUGT1 donor-negative rows are tested pairs or expanded from a general donor-preference statement
source: Retrieve the official Elsevier SI; exact-match DOI 10.1016/j.fitote.2021.104995; inspect the article's donor-selectivity section and SI Table S5; compare all 30 compilation rows and distinguish tested-pair prose from visible per-cell data
notes: Exact DOI group has 30 rows: six UDP-Glc positives and 24 zeros across four other UDP donors × six acceptors. The paper says all six acceptors were included in donor-screen experiments with UDPG and six alternative activated sugars, and reports no product for alternatives ('data not shown'); thus zeros have grouped source-reported experimental support, not merely an extrapolated specificity assumption. The 30-row compilation omits GDP-Man and GDP-Fuc, which the paper also tested. Official SI Table S5 identifies tested compounds/NP but does not show donor-specific cells. No per-cell data, LOD or replicate count found. Evidence grade: source-level report, below displayed chromatogram.

query_text: Audit source support for UGT73F17 UDP-glucuronic-acid zeros in the UGT literature compilation
source: Exact-match DOI 10.1039/C8CC04215B in the Zenodo CSV; inspect official RSC SI Methods 1.7 and Figures S13-S15; distinguish evidence that pairs were tested from evidence that their negative outcomes were shown
notes: Exact DOI group has 15 rows; three donor Glu (CID 94715, glucuronic acid) rows are zero across acceptors 1/3/6. SI Methods names UDP-GluA as tested with these acceptors, but the same recipe says UDP-Glc; Figures S13-S15 show Glc/Gal/Xyl/Ara panels without GluA outcome traces. Thus test scope is source-supported but individual inactive calls are not independently visible. Direct RSC PDF download returned 404, although official PDF text was accessible through publisher indexing. Relevance 3/3 provenance/context loss; 0/3 ML utility.

query_text: Find controlled comparisons of assay-derived inactives versus constructed decoys in molecular activity modeling
source: Search primary studies for same-model comparisons among target-specific ChEMBL inactives, DUD decoys, and mixed negative sets; inspect label thresholds, sample counts and performance metrics
notes: Czarnecki et al. (2015), DOI 10.3390/molecules201119679, compares seven-target actives-vs-ChEMBL-inactive, actives-vs-DUD, and mixed sets using the same algorithms/fingerprints. Table 5 best-fingerprint BAC is ~0.875–0.919 for measured-inactive sets versus ~0.996–1.000 for DUD sets; composition is not matched and the paper's aim is algorithm comparison. Supports benchmark-source sensitivity, not incremental measured-negative utility. Primary PMC full text: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6332304/.

query_text: Audit six UGT92G1/G2 UDP-glucuronic-acid zeros from the stratified UGT source sample
source: Exact-match DOI 10.1007/s12374-018-0103-x in the Zenodo CSV; inspect the KCI-hosted preview and primary abstract, check secondary review claims of sole UDP-glucose specificity, and verify donor CID mapping
notes: The exact DOI group has 12 rows: two enzymes × three acceptors × two UDP donors; six UDP-Glc positives and six donor-Glu zeros. CID 94715 is D-glucuronic acid. Primary abstract reports activity with UDP-glucose; a 2022 review calls UDP-glucose the sole donor. KCI exposed only a one-page preview, with no Methods/results/SI, so whether the six UDP-GlcA pairs were tested and how the compilation assigned zeros remain unresolved. Do not count as source-confirmed measured negatives. Preview retained at research/sources/ugt-donor-specificity/Rehman-2018-KCI-first-page-preview.pdf.

query_text: Audit six GuUGAT alternative UDP-sugar donor labels in the stratified UGT literature compilation
source: Exact-match DOI 10.1111/nph.14039 in the Zenodo CSV; inspect Wiley-indexed primary full-text assay methods/results; compare all six donor-acceptor rows; attempt retrieval of Fig. S14 and classify group-level versus cell-level evidence
notes: Exact DOI group has six rows: two acceptors × UDP-Glc/UDP-Gal/UDP-GlcA. Four alternative UDP-Glc/Gal cells are zero; both UDP-GlcA cells are positive. Primary methods/results text says UDP-glucose and UDP-galactose were experimentally evaluated and summarizes general specificity for UDP-GlcA, supporting the compiled zeros at group level; Fig. S14/cell values were not accessible (publisher PDF/SI endpoints blocked). Evidence grade: source-reported grouped donor comparison, not independently inspectable per-cell traces. Relevance 3/3 provenance, 0/3 direct ML utility.

query_text: Audit the RSC anthraquinone UGT source for source-panel coverage, compiled donor zeros, and omitted tested combinations
source: Exact-match DOI 10.1039/D0QO00579G in Zenodo; inspect official RSC SI Figure S9 caption for tested enzyme×donor combinations; compare the caption's full panel to all DOI-matched compilation rows; attempt SI file retrieval
notes: The exact DOI group has seven compilation rows, while official SI Figure S9 caption describes two enzymes × four UDP donors (eight combinations). Three compiled zeros (RyUGT3A/Gal, RyUGT12/Gal, RyUGT12/GlcA) and the omitted RyUGT12/UDP-GlcNAc combination are all within the source-tested panel. The SI caption confirms scope and chromatographic/LC-MS/MS product analysis, but the official PDF path returned 404, so no cell-level outcome was visually verified. The omitted result remains unknown, not imputed. Relevance 3/3 to provenance and source-vs-compilation coverage, 0/3 direct ML utility.

query_text: Summarize evidence visibility and source-versus-compilation coverage across the fixed-seed eight-paper UGT audit
source: Recompute exact DOI-field row counts from Zenodo for the eight Q106-selected sources; aggregate each article's audited negative evidence level; separate tested-panel confirmation, grouped source outcomes, cell-level figures, inaccessible sources, and omitted tested pairs
notes: Exact DOI-field matching gives 142 compiled rows (93 activity=1, 49 activity=0) across the eight selected articles. Negative evidence grades: 6 visually inspectable pair-level chromatographic outcomes; 2 explicit pair-level no-activity statements; 24 grouped no-product outcomes explicitly reported as data-not-shown; 4 zeros supported only by grouped donor-specificity prose; 7 zeros whose test scope is supported but whose outcome was not inspectable; 6 with test scope/outcome unresolved due access limits. At least one tested combination is absent from the compilation (RyUGT12/UDP-GlcNAc; T107). These counts describe only this UGT compilation sample and are not a prevalence or publication-bias estimate; one paper contributes 66 rows. No model benefit was tested.

query_text: Audit the Raccuglia et al. failed-experiment precedent for failure-label semantics, data provenance, and prospective model utility
source: Inspect the primary Nature article and author-hosted full-text PDF; recover dataset size, failure/success encoding, source of records, validation design, prospective outcome and data-quality audit; attempt official supplementary CSV retrieval
notes: Raccuglia et al. report 3,955 complete archived notebook reactions, after excluding incomplete records; score 1 (no solid) and 2 (amorphous solid) were merged as failure, while scores 3/4 were success, separate from product-purity score. Data entry was about 50 reactions/hour; random audit of 100 reactions found 34 errors among 1,800 fields (1.89%). Historical SVM average split accuracy was 74%; 34 newly selected diamines were used in prospective model-versus-human experiments, with 89% vs 78% crystal-formation success (reported p<0.05). The primary text notes historical split tests exploration but the prospective test was exploitation. Nature lists separate historical and prospective CSVs, but official Springer static endpoints returned 403, so exact failure counts and raw-field audit remain unverified. Relevance 3/3 to failure-data utility/context design, 1/3 to literature recovery, 0/3 direct molecular bioactivity transfer.

query_text: Audit the 2025 negative-chemical-data language-model study for negative provenance, label semantics, comparative design, effect size, and reproduction access
source: Read primary Science Advances article and supplementary references; distinguish constructed RegioSQM negatives from measured HiTEA yields; extract train/eval counts and metrics; inspect official code/data release and compare the claim to literature-mined molecular negative data
notes: Toniato et al. (2025), DOI 10.1126/sciadv.adt5578, directly tests reaction-model utility with (i) RegioSQM incorrect-regioisomer negatives created by moving the halogen and (ii) real HiTEA HTE observations thresholded at UV-area yield >1% positive / all others negative. In RegioSQM low-positive training, 22 positives plus 748 negatives gave positive accuracy 58.55 vs 54.91 for RL vs FT on the RegioSQM evaluation; in HiTEA, validation positive accuracy 0.644±0.015 vs 0.610±0.018 and top-10 test 0.441 vs 0.427. The authors report only 9/130 high-yield reactions had a low-yield counterpart with identical left-hand-side reactants; authors note low-but-nonzero yields and RL instability. Public Zenodo/GitHub code exists, but exact independent reproduction feasibility and data links require next-stage audit. Relevance 3/3 reaction-model utility, 2/3 label/context design, 0/3 literature-extraction and direct bioactivity transfer.

query_text: Verify the provenance, publication status, data claims, and registered DOI of the Nullary 2026 measured-negative bioactivity technical report
source: Inspect the report-hosting site and full text; classify it as peer-reviewed paper/preprint/company technical report; independently resolve its claimed Zenodo DOI via doi.org, DataCite API and Zenodo API; separate self-reported dataset/model results from verified evidence
notes: Nullary's own research page and self-hosted 8-page technical report claim a 122.3M multimodal negative-results layer and a 25-kinase measured-inactive model study (ChEMBL35). It self-reports a scaffold-split measured-negative-vs-decoy median paired ROC-AUC advantage +0.031, shrinking to +0.014 under temporal split; 1–10 µM labels are excluded and AVE-debiasing/manual source audit are acknowledged as open. The source identifies itself as a company technical report, not a peer-reviewed article. Its claimed Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20370264 returns 404 from doi.org, api.datacite.org/dois, and zenodo.org/api/records as of 2026-09-30. Treat as unverified gray-literature lead, not an independently validated prior-art result. Local report PDF retained; no underlying database accessed.

query_text: Assess whether the public Toniato et al. negative-reaction-learning repository supports a bounded reproduction on the available Blackwell GPU
source: Inspect author-pinned dependencies, public scripts/data layout and tests; verify GPU/runtime compatibility; create a project-local compatibility environment only; run bounded unit-test subset and document blockers without claiming paper-result reproduction
notes: The author pin torch==2.1.2, transformers==4.30.2, Lightning==1.9.5 and rdkit-pypi==2021.9.2. Existing RTX 5070 Ti runtime is torch 2.11.0+cu128; configured index has no rdkit-pypi 2021.9.2 or scikit-learn 1.4.1, so project-local substitutes were used. CUDA-disabled selected upstream tests pass 17/17. With CUDA visible one teacher-forcing test fails because fixture tensors remain CPU while model parameters are on cuda:0. Full collection is blocked by Windows aiohttp/SSL certificate-store error in test_scorers. Missing public bin/data setup and absent base checkpoint mean no paper training or scientific result replication was done.

query_text: Audit kinase bioactivity precedent that integrates POC assay readouts and validates predicted inactive interactions
source: Read Theisen et al. 2024 primary article and methods; quantify inferred POC labels, train-data comparison, split/evaluation design and prospective inactive assay; determine whether it extracts literature negatives or isolates negative-example utility
notes: Theisen et al. Nature Communications 15, 7596 (DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-52055-5) maps single-dose percentage-inhibition readouts to IC50-like pActivity, inferring labels for about 70,000 compound-kinase pairs with POC in >=2 concentration bins but no IC50/Ki/Kd. It compares five models trained on measured-only versus measured+inferred labels; a supplemental 10-fold cluster comparison of pairwise kernel and one deep model reports improvement in 57/60 evaluations. Separately, they experimentally profiled 50 predicted-low-activity pairs and reported NPV 78%, defining inactive as <=25% inhibition at 1,000 nM. This is direct bioactivity/readout-integration prior art but not explicit negative-statement extraction; the gain also reflects expanded data and inferred label composition, so it does not isolate negative examples' independent effect. Code/data links are public; an earlier bioRxiv manuscript PDF is retained locally, while the final publisher PDF endpoint returned HTML in this session.

query_text: Audit provenance/context fields in Theisen et al.'s released kinase activity model tables
source: Inspect author data repository at a pinned commit; count rows and measured/inferred labels; test paper-defined pActivity inactivity threshold against released values; enumerate directly available assay/source/context columns without extrapolating to unseen upstream files
notes: At GitHub commit c185bedde8a7081045bc8414906a5775f4271a1c, the prepared activity table contains 210,862 rows: 141,193 measured and 69,669 inferred. Applying pActivity<=6 yields 57,606 measured and 60,877 inferred rows on the inactive side; the inferred-side proportion is 87.4%. The POC table has 16,514 rows, 8,348 unique SMILES and 423 UniProt IDs. The published model-ready CSV schemas expose structure/protein/value/activity_type/splits and binned concentration fields, but no per-row assay ID, source DOI, relation operator or full assay context. These are direct table observations only; they do not show that source metadata are absent from authors' upstream files or that underlying database IDs cannot be mapped elsewhere. This supports the distinction between training labels and source-linked evidence; it does not prove a literature-recovery gap or estimate missingness prevalence.

query_text: Pilot source reconstruction for three measured compound-kinase rows in the public Theisen activity table
source: Take three exploratory measured rows; match exact canonical SMILES in ChEMBL; verify target through UniProt accession and target records; compare pActivity to ChEMBL measured pChEMBL; retrieve linked assays and documents/DOIs; distinguish exact activity matches from pair-level ambiguity
notes: Among three exploratory rows, two match individual ChEMBL activity records to rounding: P24941/CDK2 pActivity 5.9586 matches IC50 1100 nM/pChEMBL 5.96 (assay CHEMBL2353290, DOI 10.1016/j.bmcl.2013.02.007), and Q9NYY3/Plk2 pActivity 8.0883 matches IC50 8.16 nM/pChEMBL 8.09 (assay CHEMBL4143483, DOI 10.1016/j.ejmech.2017.11.058). The O60674/JAK2 row maps to structure and target but its prepared pActivity 7.5773 does not match the individual current ChEMBL measurements found (including 170 nM and 3.3 nM under DOI 10.1016/j.bmcl.2013.02.012); possible aggregation/version/source differences unresolved. One assay description says unknown origin, another gives system/readout details. n=3 is exploratory and not a match-rate estimate.

query_text: Countercheck apparent duplicate compound-target keys and split overlap in Theisen's prepared data
source: Re-audit all measured rows using exact case-sensitive (canonical SMILES, UniProt accession) keys; compare train/test intersections for ck, ligand and cluster split columns; document and withdraw any case-insensitive grouping results
notes: Initial PowerShell Group-Object used case-insensitive string comparison and falsely merged chemically distinct SMILES differing by letter case (e.g., aromatic c vs aliphatic C). Corrected Python standard-library CSV audit finds 141,193 measured rows and 141,193 exact pair keys; exact train/test intersections are zero in ck (21,178 test pairs), ligand (21,064) and cluster (26,785) splits. Initial reports of 426 duplicate keys and 101/96/41 split overlaps are withdrawn. Script and CSV outputs retained; audit only checks exact standardized SMILES + UniProt keys, not broader chemical equivalence.

query_text: Run a pre-registered-size stratified crosswalk of Theisen measured rows to ChEMBL activities, assay context and document sources; assess whether low-pActivity rows retain censoring relations
source: Select 10 measured rows per pActivity stratum by deterministic SHA-256 before querying; resolve connectivity candidates and UniProt target components; preserve each activity row, standard relation/value/unit, pChEMBL, assay description, document DOI and ChEMBL API release; classify numeric matches separately from pair-level/activity ambiguity
notes: Among the fixed 20-row pilot (10 pActivity<=6, 10 >6), 10 rows have at least one connectivity-level ChEMBL 37 pChEMBL within 0.005 of prepared pActivity (4/10 in <=6, 6/10 in >6). Five low-stratum rows have current ChEMBL records with relation > and standard value 10,000 nM; each corresponding prepared pActivity is approximately 5.0. Retained 38 activity-level rows with assay/document context. BindingDB independently corroborates same-structure/target/censored-value/source for four of these five rows; row 55045's same compound has a 611 nM PI3K-delta result, illustrating target-specific labels. These records are already in structured DBs, not incremental literature recovery. Small pilot; no population rate, exact author transformation or model utility claim. Primary article table verification pending. Detailed crosscheck CSV retained.

query_text: Expand the Theisen measured-row source crosswalk from 20 to a fixed 100-row, two-stratum audit
source: Use the same SHA-256 ranking and freeze 50 measured rows per pActivity stratum before lookup; map ChEMBL structures/UniProt components/activities; preserve per-record assay/document context; quantify numeric-value match, pair-level activity-only match, censoring relations and metadata completeness
notes: In the fixed 100-row audit, 60 rows have a current ChEMBL pChEMBL within 0.005 of prepared pActivity (28/50 pActivity<=6; 32/50 >6), 39 have target/structure activity but no numeric value match, and 1 has no ChEMBL structure candidate; API errors=0. The 210 activity rows all have assay ID/description and document ID, 146/210 have DOI. In the low stratum, 8/50 rows have at least one >10,000 nM record (14 activity records), and 7/8 prepared values are about 5.0. Deterministic stratified exploration only; not a full-table prevalence estimate, exact-source proof, or model utility test. 20-row pilot is nested and not an independent sample.

query_text: Follow up the sole 100-sample ChEMBL structure no-hit against PubChem and adjudicate the activity label semantics
source: Query exact source SMILES through PubChem PUG REST; retrieve CID/SID assay summaries; fetch raw AID CSV rows and assay descriptions for the matching UniProt target; separate outcome label, relation operator, numerical bound and source document type
notes: Source row 129369 (Q96RG2; pActivity≈5) maps by SMILES to PubChem CID 70925370/SID 336863075. Four PASK confirmatory assays return IC50 10,000 nM with Standard Relation <= and Activity Outcome Unspecified; AID metadata list SureChEMBL Patent Bioactivity Data. This is a plausible crosswalk candidate and shows a ChEMBL no-hit is not global absence, but it is not an explicit inactive label and exact attribution to the training row is unproven. Row-level API data retained.

query_text: Test whether the 39 activity-linked but numeric-value-mismatched rows in the fixed Theisen 100-row sample are compatible with per-pair IC50 aggregation
source: For current ChEMBL 37 records, calculate numeric IC50 pChEMBL arithmetic means per connectivity-level molecule candidate; keep censored relations out of point means; compare with prepared pActivity; label multi-candidate identity as unattributable; inspect primary article wording and document aggregation-operation ambiguity
notes: Of 39 rows, 6 single-candidate means are within 0.05 of prepared pActivity (4 within 0.01), 7 differ by >0.05, 23 have no numeric IC50 pChEMBL, and 3 have multiple structure candidates. This tests compatibility, not exact reconstruction: ChEMBL 37 may differ from source snapshot and author code; the article's phrase 'geometric mean of pIC50 values' is operationally ambiguous, so arithmetic mean in pIC50 space is a conventional diagnostic, not verified author behavior. No incremental-negative yield or model utility is established. Detailed note and per-row CSV retained.

query_text: Check whether prepared scalar pActivity values in rows lacking numeric pChEMBL are exact transforms of current ChEMBL censored IC50 bounds
source: For the 23 mismatch rows without numeric IC50 pChEMBL, convert each relation-coded standard_value/unit to molar, apply −log10, compare with prepared pActivity to six decimals, and preserve inequality direction rather than treating bounds as point measurements
notes: All 23 rows have at least one non-equality ChEMBL IC50 threshold whose −log10(M) value matches prepared pActivity at six decimals: 18 rows relation >, four <, one >=; source row 40079 has two matching >10,000 nM records (24 matching records total). This is strong numeric crosswalk evidence that the scalar can encode a threshold boundary, not proof of exact original source record or author intent. Since −log10 reverses inequalities, the relation is essential; do not call these definite negatives or novel literature records. Added bound-derived fields to row-level audit CSV and documented in T120 note.

query_text: Inspect whether the pinned Theisen author repository exposes the upstream activity-table construction and censoring/aggregation steps
source: Enumerate the full Git tree at commit c185bedde8a7081045bc8414906a5775f4271a1c; inspect README, tracked data files, and code paths for extraction/cleaning/aggregation of ChEMBL/PubChem measurements
notes: The tracked repository contains prepared input CSVs, model training scripts and figure scripts; README describes data as preformatted. No tracked pipeline constructs the measured activity table from source databases. This means public artifacts inspected cannot resolve how relation-coded bounds entered model-ready pActivity; absence from public tree does not imply no internal pipeline or establish an error. Relevant to reproduction boundary only; no new negative-data utility evidence.

query_text: Verify one current-ChEMBL censored CDK2 record against the cited source publication and classify source-cell confidence
source: Inspect Borzilleri et al. DOI 10.1021/jm0501275 full text, kinase-selectivity Results/Table 5 and Methods; compare target, cutoff, assay context and transformed boundary with Theisen row 7684/ChEMBL CHEMBL194498; explicitly check whether exact compound number is identified
notes: Paper text independently confirms a kinase selectivity panel and no significant CDK2 activity; Table 5 gives CDK2 IC50 >50 μM for five selected analogues, and methods describe recombinant kinase, poly(Glu4/Tyr), and radiometric filter-based assay. ChEMBL row 7684 is CDK2 IC50 >50,000 nM and prepared pActivity=4.30103, the same transformed boundary. Exact mapping to a numbered table compound was not recovered from SI in this check, so classify as target/cutoff corroboration, not unique compound-cell reconstruction. Existing ChEMBL record means no incremental recovery.

query_text: Verify a left-censored BRAF V600E IC50 and distinguish it from the same compound's cellular p-ERK endpoint in the source paper
source: For Theisen row 69665, compare CHEMBL3335372's two current ChEMBL records with Subramanian et al. DOI 10.1021/ml5002272 Table 1; convert μM/nM units; test whether the paired cell endpoint distinguishes the likely compound row; retain strict inequality semantics
notes: ChEMBL records show BRAF V600E IC50 <0.4 nM and separate cell-based BRAF-mediated p-ERK EC50=100 nM. Source Table 1 compound 9 reports <0.0004 μM and 0.1 μM, matching both; compound 10 shares the biochemical bound but has p-ERK EC50 0.05 μM, supporting compound 9 attribution. Prepared pActivity 9.397940 equals transformed cutoff, but <IC50 implies pIC50 > boundary. Direct SI structure-to-CHEMBL mapping not separately inspected. Existing ChEMBL coverage; not a negative or novel recovery.

query_text: Trace three DOI-missing censored kinase rows to patent documents and classify their source type and label semantics
source: For Theisen rows 89062, 100130 and 99152, inspect ChEMBL 37 document/assay/activity metadata and the corresponding patent activity-bin legends and assay descriptions; distinguish patent records from journal literature and preserve censoring relations
notes: Rows resolve to EphA2 IC50 <50 nM and EphB4 IC50 <50 nM in CHEMBL3882729/US20090318373A1, and c-Raf1 IC50 <100 nM in CHEMBL3882735/US7846959B2. Patent A-bin thresholds agree with the prepared pActivity censoring boundaries. All three are potent censored actives, not negatives; no DOI is not no source. Targeted n=3 follow-up, not prevalence estimate; records already in ChEMBL, no incremental literature recovery or model gain; exact compound-to-patent-cell attribution remains unverified.

query_text: Audit Bosc et al. 2019 as prior art for literature-derived, relation-coded records in large-scale bioactivity models and separate this from incremental negative-data utility
source: Read the publisher full text; verify ChEMBL_23 literature-source filters, relation-< selection, target-class thresholding, target count, QSAR/conformal comparison and reported metrics; log whether the design includes a matched with/without-censored-record ablation
notes: Bosc et al. report selecting literature-source ChEMBL activity records and additional relation-< observations for inactive-data modeling across 550 human targets; mean QSAR sensitivity/specificity/CCR are 0.80/0.81/0.81. These metrics compare QSAR with Mondrian conformal prediction, not models with versus without censored records. The work narrows broad novelty but does not isolate negative-record benefit or perform historical source-text extraction. Row-level censor-to-class validity was not independently reproduced.

query_text: Resolve the earlier LpBgl5/BRENDA coverage query using EC 3.2.1.86 and distinguish exact enzyme/observation coverage from same-organism homologs
source: Check the public BRENDA EC 3.2.1.86 page/sequence search for the LpBgl5 source protein XOT41254.1; inspect the displayed Lactiplantibacillus plantarum WCFS1 record F9UU25, compare retrieved protein sequences, and check whether any record matches the four specific unphosphorylated substrate results and 2025 source
notes: BRENDA shows a same-species, same-EC WCFS1 6-phospho-beta-glucosidase entry F9UU25/4GZE, but not the source protein accession XOT41254.1. Exploratory global alignment gives 56.53% identity, confirming only a homolog-level near-match. No exact accession-paper-substrate-result match was established for the four LpBgl5 negatives; cellobiose-6-phosphate is distinct from unphosphorylated cellobiose. Bounded page checks cannot prove database-wide absence, so do not count the observations as database-unique.

query_text: Audit field-level experimental-context completeness in the existing 14-candidate, three-paper enzyme-negative pilot, keeping source certainty, protocol context, LOD, and raw replicates distinct
source: Reconcile annotation_pilot_v0.csv against primary Methods, source tables/figures, and Heins et al. Supplementary Table 2; code each field as row-level/shared-method/missing/ambiguous and separate the four BglM dashes from confirmed negatives
notes: All 14 candidates have a source locator and recoverable entity/substrate, pH, temperature, readout, and substrate concentration after joining methods to result sources. Per-record enzyme amount and duration are available for 10/14; four BglM cells retain unresolved per-cell enzyme amount and no verified duration, and their dash outcome remains ambiguous. Replicate/control context is reported but not homogeneous. No individual raw replicate values or explicit analytical LOD were recovered; NIMS 0.1 is a negative-control-derived background threshold, not automatically an analytical LOD. Purposeful single-annotator pilot only; no prevalence, automation, database uniqueness, or model-utility claim.

query_text: Audit PAYN (Boser et al., JACS 2026) as direct prior art for organic-reaction reporting-bias simulation, PU-inferred negatives, and downstream yield-model gains; distinguish it from source-linked assay-negative extraction
source: Read the peer-reviewed primary article and the public GloriusGroup/PAYN repository README; compare target domain, observed versus inferred labels, bias evaluation design, context/provenance retention, and author-reported results with Janus claims
notes: PAYN masks negative outcomes in fully labelled HTE reaction data to form PU training sets, infers reliable negatives by a spy technique, and reports lower yield-regression MAE than positives-only baselines across multiple reaction sets. This is direct prior art for inferred-negative supplementation and model value in reaction prediction; it does not mine explicit source-paper negatives or quantify actual publication missingness. The audit did not run code or reproduce metrics. Relevance 3/3 to broad novelty boundary; adjacent to protein-bioactivity literature extraction.

query_text: Audit the reproducibility boundary of PAYN's public code, tracked data, default split and test/tuning flow; verify executable tests before choosing a metric-reproduction scope
source: Pin repository HEAD; inspect pyproject/config/run_spy, experiments README, core split/optimization/recombination paths and tracked workbook dimensions; create isolated Python 3.12 environment, import main entry point and run repository pytest without changing the clone
notes: At pinned HEAD e3f12fde506d1adfc0a178eb87b5f21a8f4a0ed8, main entry imports and 130 tests pass. Default main uses shuffled random row KFold, validation-set optimization and fixed inferred-negative yield; no test-label use in the optimization objective was found. Only two benchmark-sized workbooks (3,955 and 5,760 rows) are tracked, not all four paper sets; legacy scripts are explicitly marked potentially stale. No paper-level model result reproduced. Follow-up should run a bounded Ahneman smoke test before deciding on full 5-fold/50-trial replication.

query_text: Run one bounded PAYN pipeline fold on the tracked 3,955-row reaction matrix; verify runtime feasibility, hidden-label RN precision and directional downstream test MAE without calling it a paper reproduction
source: Run author featurisation, one outer split, PU split/spy infiltration, 100-tree spy CatBoost, RN identification, fixed-zero-yield recombination and 100-tree positive-only/augmented regression with no Optuna search; keep true labels out of RN inference and use them only afterward for evaluation
notes: First fold n_train/val/test=2847/317/791; PAYN selected 342 inferred RNs with hidden-label precision 92.98%; test MAE 14.134 positive-only vs 7.479 augmented. One-fold smoke only: lower MAE is confounded by larger/changed training set, no repeated folds or matched-size/random-negative controls, and parameters/versions differ from paper. pandas 3.0.6 failed at assigning string role labels into float columns, while pandas 2.2.3 completed with a FutureWarning. Do not cite this as reproducing published metrics; next priority remains source-confirmed bioactivity/enzyme negatives, exact database overlap, and blinded annotation.

query_text: Determine whether SABIO-RK contains the exact source/condition-specific Q25BW5 BGL1A–cellobiose negatives in the enzyme pilot, distinguishing exact observation overlap from same protein/substrate records under other conditions
source: Query the current SABIO-RK API by exact UniProt accession Q25BW5 with rows=100; parse all returned entry JSON for paper/PMID, protein variant, reaction substrate, pH, temperature, kinetic parameters and compare against NP009–NP014 Heins 2014 source conditions
notes: API returned 13 records, all linked to PMID 18023045 (one 2008 paper) and Q25BW5/BGL1A-cellobiose hydrolysis; pH-dependent positive kinetic-law entries are listed at 30 C. None of the returned entries establishes the six Heins 2014 <0.1 observations at pH 5/8 and 60/80/90 C. Adjudicate as same exact protein/substrate, different source/conditions; exact Heins-observation match not established, database-wide absence not claimed. Full row decisions NP001–NP015 in database_coverage_adjudication_v0.csv. Relevance 3/3; supports context-sensitive exact-overlap design, not overall coverage rate or ML gain.

query_text: Audit cross-paper wording for the exact Phanerochaete chrysosporium BGL1A–cellobiose system to determine whether lower activity, a prose no-hydrolysis claim, and curated kinetic values can be normalized to one binary outcome
source: Compare PubMed abstracts for Tsukada 2006 (PMID 16896601), Nijikken 2007 (PMID 17376440), Tsukada 2008 (PMID 18023045), and SABIO-RK Q25BW5 entry conditions/kinetic fields; explicitly check whether matched LOD and assay protocols justify calling the source statements contradictory
notes: 2006 abstract says BGL1A hydrolyzes cellobiose less effectively than BGL1B; 2007 abstract says BGL1A does not; 2008 abstract and SABIO-RK expose pH-dependent BGL1A/mutant cellobiose kinetics. Abstract/API review does not establish harmonized assay conditions, LOD, or the operational sense of 'does not'; record as source-wording mismatch, not a proven experimental contradiction. Implication: preserve original statement, threshold/LOD, conditions and normalized-label uncertainty separately. Does not establish prevalence or ML utility. Relevance 3/3.

query_text: Re-read the full-text BglM-G1 Results/Table 1 context to establish which alpha-substrate no-detect statements can be assigned to wild type versus H75R rather than treating four dashes identically
source: Inspect the section heading/paragraph subject, Table 1 substrate rows and variant columns, subsequent H75R subsection, and Methods context; map scope conservatively to NP005–NP008
notes: The statement that no tested alpha-glycosidic substrate activity was detected occurs in the BglM-G1-specific Results subsection; Table 1 lists alpha-arabinofuranoside and alpha-rhamnopyranoside. Reclassify wild-type NP005/NP007 as source-confirmed qualitative panel-level non-detects, not numeric zeros. The statement is not explicitly extended to H75R, introduced later; NP006/NP008 remain ambiguous table dashes despite a broad 'comparable substrate specificities' description. No database crosswalk attempted. Relevance 3/3; improves recall while controlling variant-level over-propagation.

query_text: Crosswalk the two full-text-confirmed BglM-G1 alpha-D substrate non-detections against live BRENDA/SABIO-RK records, separating exact source/entity matches from L-stereoisomer or other-enzyme near-matches
source: Query SABIO-RK exact/free-text identifiers and all 445 EC 3.2.1.21 records; inspect the public BRENDA EC 3.2.1.21 page for BglM-G1/KRO51423/DOI and exact alpha-D substrate names versus visible analog records
notes: SABIO-RK exact accession/name/PMID/substrate/free-text queries returned 0; broad EC 3.2.1.21 returned 445 records and did not expose BglM-G1, the article, or exact D-configured test substrates. BRENDA live EC page contained no BglM-G1/KRO51423/DOI/Mhaindarkar strings; visible near-name pNP alpha-L-arabinofuranoside and alpha-L-rhamnopyranoside entries are not the source's alpha-D substrates. No exact source-observation match established in scoped searches; do not claim global absence. NP005/NP007 remain source-confirmed panel-level qualitative negatives; NP006/NP008 remain ambiguous. Relevance 3/3; candidate incremental evidence only, no prevalence/model gain.

query_text: Determine whether recent work already combines literature-derived molecular assay context, structured evidence provenance, validation, and downstream model utility, and whether it addresses negative outcomes
source: Search primary/preprint sources published by 2026-10-01 for recent BindingDB literature-context extraction; inspect Assay-Aware BindingDB full text for dataset unit, source-span method, ontology, expert evaluation, model split/results, outcome-label scope, and peer-review status
notes: Assay-Aware BindingDB (arXiv:2609.34001v1, submitted 2026-09-27) reports 74,425 BindingDB protein–ligand affinity pairs with four-assay context, a two-stage evidence-span/ontology pipeline, expert-reference evaluation on 120 papers, and author-reported paper-held-out Boltz-2 gains. Its declared task is context-aware affinity prediction, not source-grounded negative/no-detect/censored-outcome extraction; no matched test of negative observations is reported. Preprint only, not independently reproduced. Relevance 3/3: rejects generic context-extraction/model-gain novelty, leaves negative-observation recovery and incremental database coverage untested.

query_text: Assess a recent protein–ligand ML paper that uses experimentally inactive bioactivity records alongside decoys, focusing on what it actually proves about negative data scarcity and utility
source: Inspect Schottlender et al. 2025 full Methods/Results/Discussion for ChEMBL inactive thresholds/comments, decoy matching, model evaluation design, negative-specific ablation, and authors' statement about negative-data scarcity
notes: The peer-reviewed BSI paper defines ChEMBL v33 pChEMBL >6.5 as active and <4.5 as experimentally inactive, supplements with target-specific property-matched DUD-E decoys, and reports BSI performance over the combined S/N construction. It explicitly calls reliable negatives scarce, but does not report a matched ablation replacing measured inactives with decoys/assumed negatives; model gains cannot be attributed specifically to measured negatives. It queries ChEMBL rather than mining literature source evidence. Relevance 2/3; informative precedent and gap, not a direct estimate of negative-data causal utility.

query_text: Test whether inferred low-activity kinase labels have utility beyond merely changing training-set size, and assess relevance to source-grounded negative-data aims
source: Run paired fixed-budget replacement ablations at N=2,000 and 8,000 over three supplied splits and five seeds; compare inferred pActivity≤6 with measured-row replacement and inferred >6 controls; document scope limits
notes: The low-inferred arm raises held-out measured inactive recall in all six split/budget settings but worsens MAE and lowers precision in all six; F1/balanced-accuracy shifts are small and split-dependent. These are model-inferred POC-derived labels, not literature-source-confirmed negatives; this replacement design does not test adding source-grounded negatives. Relevance 2/3: informs matched-ablation design, not Janus extraction or negative-data utility directly.

query_text: Map prior art for literature mining of negative biological evidence and determine whether it covers molecular activity outcomes
source: Search primary records for text-mined negative interaction databases; read Negatome 2.0 methods/evaluation and ChEMBL direct-deposition paper's rationale on supplementary and negative data; compare units, evidence types, and validation to Janus
notes: Negatome 2.0 (2014) used text mining to guide manual curation of protein non-interactions, with reported precision/recall limitations and 2,171 manually curated literature pairs; it is a methodological prior art, not bioactivity extraction. ChEMBL direct-deposition authors explicitly identify supplementary and negative results as potentially absent from papers, but provide no prevalence estimate. Relevance 2/3 to method/problem framing, not direct activity evidence.

query_text: Audit the closest structured-data counterexample to a claim that assay-contextualized molecular negatives are unavailable
source: Read the ECBD primary article for tested-panel scope, negative/result call schema, endpoint/assay context, release/embargo snapshot, source pathway, and external database links; define what ECBD does and does not settle for retrospective literature recovery
notes: ECBD reports full EU-OPENSCREEN campaign data with per-compound active/inconclusive/inactive/error/undefined calls, numeric endpoints, protocol/context metadata, and primary/confirmatory/counter-screen coverage; Aug 2024 paper snapshot: 89 submissions (48 public), ~4.32M endpoints and ~2.40M results overall. It is a strong existing resource but not retrospective literature mining or a measurement of publication bias. Relevance 3/3; Janus must test exact historical incremental coverage.

query_text: Cross-check the 14 source-linked enzyme pilot observations against ChEMBL, PubChem BioAssay, and ECBD; distinguish exact source-observation matches from lexical or entity near-matches
source: Query ChEMBL document endpoint by each DOI and PMID; search PubChem BioAssay Entrez by exact DOI, protein/accession and substrate terms and inspect hit AID descriptions; paginate all currently exposed ECBD assay/target records for source/entity terms; run known DOI/PMID/AID/assay-name positive controls; record limits and avoid global-absence claims
notes: No DOI- or PMID-exact ChEMBL document and no exact PubChem source/entity string was found. ECBD scan of 173 public assay objects and 35 target objects returned no candidate-source/entity strings, but did not scan 110,968 compound-result records. PubChem cellobiose/hydrolysis keywords yielded nine unrelated 2011 maltose intestinal-glycosidase assays. Known DOI/PMID controls in ChEMBL, known DOI/AID controls in PubChem, and ECBD assay-name control were recovered; this confirms basic paths, not full sensitivity. PubChem Entrez pcassay exposes no PMID search field, so no PMID-negative claim is made. Conclusion only: exact coverage not established in scoped queries; lexical hits are insufficient. Relevance 3/3 to pilot feasibility, not prevalence.

query_text: Audit PubChem BioAssay target-field sensitivity and identifier-version effects before interpreting pilot protein/accession no-hits
source: Use AID 1000 as a known target positive control; retrieve its PUG REST target metadata; query Entrez by typed protein-name [PTN], GI [PTGI], and GenBank accession [GBAC] fields; contrast versionless/versioned accession forms; re-run the pilot candidate accessions in their typed fields
notes: AID 1000 resolves to GI 116516899 and mevalonate kinase. Entrez returned 8 results for mevalonate kinase [PTN], 3 for 116516899 [PTGI], 3 AIDs (1000/557/555) for versionless YP_815859 [GBAC], but zero for YP_815859.1 [GBAC]. Typed candidate queries XOT41254 [GBAC], XOT41254.1 [GBAC], KRO51423 [GBAC], KRO51423 [UPAC], Q25BW5 [UPAC], BAE87008 [GBAC], and BAE87008.1 [GBAC] returned zero. This strengthens the scoped no-hit audit but does not establish biological/database absence; one target-family control is not global sensitivity. Relevance 3/3 to reliable incremental-coverage assessment.

query_text: Resolve whether PubChem represents the four pilot enzyme accessions as protein entities and whether any are linked to BioAssay AIDs
source: Call documented PUG REST protein accession summary, protein-to-AIDs, and direct assay-target-by-accession AIDs endpoints for XOT41254, KRO51423, Q25BW5, and BAE87008; use YP_815859 as a positive control for both target-to-assay routes; manually verify Q25BW5 protein name and taxonomy against the pilot source
notes: Q25BW5 resolves to beta-glucosidase 1A, Phanerochaete chrysosporium, but both its protein-linked AIDs and direct assay-target AIDs endpoints return no AID data. XOT41254, KRO51423, and BAE87008 return no protein summary and no AIDs. Positive-control YP_815859 returns AIDs 555, 557, 1000 through both routes. Thus the exact protein entity is represented for J037, but two queried protein-to-BioAssay paths did not identify a linked experiment; this is not proof that all alternate target/assay links are absent. Relevance 3/3 because exact observation coverage requires assay-result evidence, not merely a protein page.

query_text: Probe a denominator-defined retrospective enzyme-paper sampling frame that can quantify how often published enzyme specificity papers expose negative observations
source: Run three PubMed title/abstract searches limited to 2015-2025: beta-glucosidase AND substrate specificity; glycoside hydrolase family 1 AND substrate specificity; beta-glucosidase AND (substrate range OR substrate screening); record exact query translations and counts; merge PubMed IDs and calculate the deduplicated candidate pool
notes: PubMed returned 73, 12, and 3 records respectively; the union is 80 unique PubMed IDs from 88 total hits (8 duplicate hits). This is still a lexical candidate pool, not an eligible-paper denominator: primary-study status, experimental substrate-panel scope, full-text/supplement access, and extractable negative outcomes remain unscreened. It provides a bounded candidate cohort for screening but cannot estimate field-wide publication bias. Relevance 3/3 to building a transparent feasibility denominator.

query_text: Pilot title/abstract screening of the 80-record beta-glucosidase specificity candidate frame; identify indexing-label conflicts and off-scope query noise
source: Fetch PubMed title, abstract, publication type and PMID metadata for the deduplicated union; inspect boundary candidates including reviews, in-silico papers, community/environmental assays and other GH enzymes; re-open PMID 32522206 at PMC after PubMed labels it Review and compare metadata with article methods/results
date: Initial screen identified four clearly review-like records plus PMID 32522206, which PubMed tags Review but whose PMC full text reports heterologous expression, purification, kinetic characterization and enzyme-engineering experiments. Other evident noise includes in-silico ligand binding, wastewater/soil/metabarcoding studies and non-beta-glucosidase enzymes. The discrepancy means publication type alone cannot be used as the exclusion rule. This is a boundary-case pilot only: no complete 80-record disposition or eligible denominator is claimed. Relevance 3/3 to validity of the planned sample frame.

query_text: Full-text adjudicate an apparent Review-tagged beta-glucosidase specificity paper and code its weak-activity statements without converting them to zero
source: Retrieve the PMC JATS XML for PMID 32522206; inspect Results, Table 1 and Methods sections on BGL-1 substrate specificity; extract exact units, comparative outcomes, assay conditions, replicate statement and whether the 10 U/mg boundary is declared as LOD; compare PubMed publication type with the primary article content
date: Despite PubMed's Review tag, the article reports recombinant expression, purification, kinetic assays and E521G/E521S engineering and qualifies as an experimental candidate. It calls laminaribiose/gentiobiose activity negligible below 10 U/mg; cellobiose and sophorose activities are 110.27±4.38 and 535.82±15.83 U/mg. The four disaccharides were tested at 10 mM, 100 mM sodium acetate pH 4, 60 C, 10 min, glucose release by Glucose-TR, with triplicates reported generally; the inspected method does not define 10 U/mg as LOD or give the exact enzyme amount. Cellooligosaccharide activity described as lower than GH3 is relative, while Table 1 reports measurable kinetic values. Relevance 3/3 to negative-label semantics and sample eligibility; not evidence of model utility or prevalence.

query_text: Screen a continuous 25-record PMID-sorted tranche from the beta-glucosidase specificity candidate frame and retain per-record decisions
source: For PubMed-ID-sorted candidate positions 36-60 (PMIDs 32207174–37055368), compare title/abstract/publication type to the prespecified narrow rule: primary experimental study, defined beta-glucosidase or variant, and substrate-specificity activity comparison; mark out-of-target enzymes, community-level studies and reviews as exclusions; fetch full abstracts for three uncertain papers
date: Of 25 records, 12 were sent to full-text review, PMID 32522206 was full-text confirmed eligible, 11 were excluded at title/abstract stage for review/off-target enzyme/community or non-target study design, and PMID 35723691 remains unclear pending full text for a measured multi-substrate panel. Decisions and short reasons saved in beta-glucosidase-screening-log.csv. This is a contiguous screening tranche, not a random estimate and not the final eligible denominator. Relevance 3/3 to a denominator-defined feasibility cohort.

query_text: Broad cross-domain search for public negative-data resources in molecular science, biomedicine, reactions, and materials
source: Search combinations of negative-results database, experimentally confirmed inactive, failed synthesis, material screening, molecular benchmark, cross-domain biomedical negative resource; follow primary dataset cards and repository documentation rather than secondary commentary
date: Surfaced NegBioDB as a public five-domain biomedical resource/benchmark and Scandium Labs SSB as a materials dataset with an explicit computational negative-result field and unknown state. Search establishes candidate prior-art resources, not peer-reviewed status or verified record semantics. Relevance 3/3 to resource novelty; follow-up source audit needed.

query_text: Source-level audit of newly surfaced cross-domain negative resources
source: Inspect NegBioDB public dataset card and configuration for source lists, DTI thresholds, counts, and parent-project accessibility; inspect Scandium repository release notes and technical documentation for negative label rules, unknown handling, and dataset composition
date: NegBioDB config states IC50/Ki/Kd >10 μM inactivity and pChEMBL ≥6 activity with borderline exclusion; card overview DTI-negative count (30,459,583) differs from the listed ~25M DTI parquet. Scandium docs define computational proxies (energy above hull, metallicity, Li hopping distance) and leave uncomputable cases None. Neither was independently reproduced or row-audited; the former is not demonstrated to extract historical paper evidence and the latter is not experimental failure/inactivity. Relevance 3/3 to ontology/prior-art boundaries.
